answer: One concrete sybil defense is bonded staking with slashing. Each agent locks a deposit before joining a task market, so minting a fake identity costs a fresh full bond and a sybil army becomes linearly expensive. If a dispute proves two accounts were driven by one operator, a challenge panel burns both bonds and pays the slash to the honest reporter. Every credential thus anchors to real locked value, and cheap duplication fails. A supplier hauling ivory across a mesa toward a harbor must collateralize each route claim the same way: scarce capital, not free usernames, pins down every identity.
